summary: Performed a sweeping audit for residual Unity/extension coupling across the app, server, packages, and docs. Reported six remaining leak categories: stale `activeDomains`/`domainId` terminology, single global project-service model, Unity-specific settings in core, extension-specific CSS selectors in core, Unity-shaped generic APIs, and minor stale strings.
decisions: Rename `activeDomains`/`domainId` toward `enabledExtensionIds` while retaining protocol migration compatibility.
Scope project `open`/`status` operations by extension rather than the current single-owner design (e.g., replace `CompositeProjectService.#first()`, `hasProjectStatus`, `store.projectStatus`).
Move `compilePlayModePolicy` out of core app settings and `WorkspaceLayout` into extension-owned persisted settings.
Relocate extension-specific CSS (panel IDs like `unity`/`git`/`activity` and Unity diagnostic selectors) from core stylesheets into extension bundles; core retains only generic panel primitives.
Generalize Unity-shaped APIs (`UnityStatus`, `UnityOpenProjectResult`, Unity parsers, related client errors) into generic project/workspace contracts, keeping Unity types inside the Unity extension.
Fix `GitCapability`'s stale 'No Unity project is selected.' string.
Treat the retained `showUnityInspector` references as intentional migration-only compatibility shims.
